name: Pansori
lineage: Korean epic-narrative solo-vocal tradition with single sorikkun (singer-storyteller) accompanied by single buk barrel-drum gosu (drummer) and aniri spoken-narration interludes between sung passages. Codified late-17th-and-18th-century onward in Cholla-province (southwestern Korean peninsula) from earlier shamanic kut-ritual narrative-chant, evolved through 19th-century master-disciple-school lineages into a 3-to-8-hour concert form covering twelve canonical madang epic-narratives (now five surviving: Chunhyangga, Simcheongga, Heungbuga, Sugungga, Jeokbyeokga). The vocal technique stresses sangchung-cheong middle-register, jjokbal-hoek tonal-coloration, and gyeongdrumeokpan throat-tearing rough-vocal-quality (deliberately broken via years of practice), with strict jangdan rhythmic-cycle alternation from slowest 18/8 jinyangjo to fastest 4/4 hwimori.
